title: Us-vs-Them bias in Large Language Models
findings: When conditioned on a 'Conservative' persona in a U.S. political context, LLMs generated outgroup sentences that associated the 'other' with 'undermining religious freedoms by attacking Christian values and promoting secularism in schools.' In contrast, the 'Liberal' persona generated ingroup sentences promoting 'social justice and equality for all, regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, or religion.' This demonstrates that religion is used as a thematic element to construct 'us vs. them' bias differently depending on the political persona.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures 'us versus them' bias in LLM-generated sentences. Religion is one of the dimensions of this bias, with specific analysis on how political personas (Conservative vs. Liberal) frame religious topics, such as the Conservative persona's association of the outgroup with 'undermining religious freedoms by attacking Christian values'.
